gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noto-sans-myanmar: A slit of an opening where the c nearly shuts gives Groovy its funk. Noto Sans Myanmar follows with a dense, heavy-looking strip of text and a broad c, so a long read feels solid and friendly.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noto-sans-nabataean: Groovy draws flat, contrast-free letterforms with a loose, playful spacing that feels friendly right away. And Noto Sans Nabataean, with lowercase almost as tall as its capitals and generous s curves, keeps a long read moving smoothly.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noto-sans-nag-munda: Closed, narrow-mouthed letters give Groovy its funky face. Noto Sans Nag Mundari opens its curves wide and lets lowercase rival the capitals, so a longer passage reads in a modern, easygoing way.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noto-sans-nandinaga: Noto Sans Nandinagari keeps its openings generous at every weight, with short ascenders and a big lowercase body. Groovy, meanwhile, stays thin-looking and funky above it.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noto-sans-newa: Groovy looks drawn with a round-tipped pen, its letters closed up and playfully tight with no thin spots anywhere. Noto Sans Newa opens its e and stretches its bowls tall, which is the pair's whole charm.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noto-sans-nushu: Noto Sans Nushu holds its terminals far from the stroke and towers with a big x-height, a modern, contemporary look. Groovy, closed and funky, sits against it nicely.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noto-sans-ogham: Noto Sans Ogham reads as bold lowercase because the bodies run so tall, with wide gaps in the e. Groovy's fixed-nib strokes make a cheerful, quirky partner above it.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noto-sans-ol-chiki: Friendly and funky, Groovy tightens its letters into near-closed shapes. Noto Sans Ol Chiki holds its curve tails well back, so words form solid blocks, and that clean contrast is the pair's strongest quality.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noto-sans-old-hunga: Quirky up top, spacious below: Groovy keeps its stroke widths fixed from stem to curve while closed up tight. Noto Sans Old Hungarian opens its counters wide, and that openness is the pair's strongest quality.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noto-sans-old-itali: Noto Sans Old Italic sits with almost no gap between x-height and cap height, and its curve endings stay well apart. And Groovy, closed and pinch-free, makes a long stretch of that body read smoothly.
